findings.reasoning: All visible headers are snake_case. None are cryptic single-token headers like dt, id, val, vol, num, qty, col1, or flag; instrument_id is qualified, and the other names are descriptive.

findings.title: Data quality validation present
findings.evidence: Risk_Pipeline/01_IngestMarketData.py contains the data checks before writing silver/InstrumentReturns_20240314.csv.
findings.reasoning: The repository contains multiple data-loading and transformation steps, and the visible pipeline files include explicit validation before use: the ingest script asserts positive prices and no duplicate rows before feature engineering. At the repository level there is no missing cross-file quality gate to report beyond what is already visible in the single file review.

findings.title: Logging and monitoring
findings.evidence: Risk_Pipeline/01_IngestMarketData.py configures logs/ingest.log, and the pipeline writes CSV outputs in Risk_Pipeline/01_IngestMarketData.py and Risk_Pipeline/02_VolatilityModel.py.
findings.reasoning: The pipeline jobs do leave persistent logs via the logging module in the ingest stage, and the training step prints metrics but is not the only persistence mechanism because the job writes a CSV artifact. There is no repository-level inconsistency showing a missing outliving record across files.

findings.title: No hardcoded secrets or credentials
findings.evidence: Risk_Pipeline/03_ComputeVaR.py contains the literal API key assignment.
findings.reasoning: A hardcoded API key literal appears in the VaR computation script, but that evidence is entirely contained within a single file and is already visible to per-file review; there is no additional repository-level inconsistency to add.

findings.title: No raw PII exposed in outputs
findings.evidence: data/trader_contacts.csv exposes contact-related columns in its header.
findings.reasoning: The repository includes a CSV header with direct identifier fields for trader contact data, but this is a single-file exposure rather than a cross-file inconsistency. No additional repository-level issue beyond the visible file content is present.

findings.title: Random seeds fixed for stochastic steps
findings.evidence: Risk_Pipeline/02_VolatilityModel.py uses train_test_split without any seed in the file.
findings.reasoning: The only stochastic step is train_test_split in the volatility model, and there is no seed set in that file. However, that is a file-local reproducibility issue already visible in the file itself, not a repository-level inconsistency.

findings.title: Shared output table grain documentation
findings.evidence: README.md, Risk_Pipeline/03_ComputeVaR.py, and Risk_SQL/CreateVarBreachFact.sql do not state the row grain for gold/DailyVaRReport_20240314.csv or Reporting.VarBreachFact.  Quoted: 'Daily VaR breach fact table'
findings.reasoning: This repository does contain a gold output path and a Fact table DDL, so the policy applies. The gold/reporting output is gold/DailyVaRReport_20240314.csv, and the table definition is Reporting.VarBreachFact. The README, pipeline docstrings/comments, and SQL DDL do not state what one row represents for either output, so the repository lacks the required grain documentation.

remediation.description: Add explicit row-grain documentation for the Daily VaR breach fact outputs in the README and the two pipeline/SQL files.

findings.title: Git branching and commit standards
findings.evidence: azure-pipelines.yml configures an unsupported branch name in the trigger list.  Quoted: '- hotfix-var-breach-mar24'  [not counted at repository level: already reported by the per-file pass]
findings.reasoning: The branch configuration includes master and develop, but also hotfix-var-breach-mar24, which is not an allowed branch name under the rule. The PR settings also require at least one reviewer, but the branch-name violation remains.

findings.title: SQL table and object naming convention
findings.evidence: Risk_SQL/CreateVarBreachFact.sql defines Reporting.VarBreachFact.
findings.reasoning: The SQL object definition uses an approved schema and a PascalCase table name with a Fact suffix, and no Hungarian prefixes or other naming violations are present at the repository level. There is no cross-file inconsistency to report.

findings.title: SQL column naming convention
findings.evidence: Risk_SQL/CreateVarBreachFact.sql uses PascalCase column names such as VarBreachKey and RiskLimitAmount.
findings.reasoning: The SQL table columns are PascalCase and appropriately qualified, and there is no repository-level mismatch between DataFrame columns destined for SQL and the SQL DDL. No additional issue appears across files.

findings.title: Medallion architecture (Bronze / Silver / Gold)
findings.evidence: Risk_Pipeline/01_IngestMarketData.py writes silver/InstrumentReturns_20240314.csv after checks, and Risk_Pipeline/03_ComputeVaR.py writes gold/DailyVaRReport_20240314.csv from silver data.
findings.reasoning: The repository follows bronze to silver to gold flow: raw bronze inputs are validated before writing silver, and silver outputs are later written to gold. There is no repository-level layer skip or missing middle-layer validation beyond what is already visible in the pipeline files.

findings.title: Raw source data not modified in place
findings.evidence: Risk_Pipeline/01_IngestMarketData.py reads bronze/MarketDataFeed_20240314.csv and writes silver/InstrumentReturns_20240314.csv, while Risk_Pipeline/03_ComputeVaR.py reads bronze/TradingPositions_20240314.csv and writes gold/DailyVaRReport_20240314.csv.
findings.reasoning: No file writes back over the same raw path it reads; bronze inputs are read and silver or gold outputs are written elsewhere. There is no repository-level in-place modification of raw source data.
